Higher-frequency ultrasound waves experience greater attenuation and are absorbed more strongly by tissue, which reduces their penetration depth. In contrast, lower-frequency waves can travel further into tissue with less loss of energy. This is because higher frequencies have a shorter wavelength, making them more susceptible to absorption by tissue components.
